{"created":"2024-03-20 (follow-up of INC-2024-0312)","domain":"databases","escalation":"Infrastructure team when the value at fault belongs to an object only they deploy: DBProxy, load balancer, NAT Gateway.","id":"RB-014","procedure":"1. Read app_heap_bytes and db_connection_wait_seconds over the same window. If the connection wait grows together with the RSS, memory is a symptom, not the cause.
2. Read the application container logs. 'connection reset by peer' means a close SUFFERED: the other end hung up. A 'timeout' would mean the opposite, a wait abandoned by the application. That nuance drives everything that follows.
3. List EVERY element of the network path able to close an idle connection, with its value: RDS Proxy (idleClientTimeout field of the DBProxy resource), NAT Gateway, load balancer (idle timeout), service mesh, stateful firewall. Each carries its own value and none knows the others'.
4. Compare the SHORTEST of these values with the idle connection recycling delay of the application pool. The latter is logged at pod start (line 'db pool ... idle_timeout=') and set by the DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS variable. GENERAL RULE: the pool must recycle BEFORE the most impatient element of the path. AWS writes it for RDS Proxy: 'configure your pool with an idle connection timeout of a value lower than your client connection idle timeout setting for RDS Proxy to avoid unexpected connection drops'.
5. If the relation is inverted, that is the cause. Fix ONE of the two values: lower the pool recycling below the network threshold, or raise the network threshold above the recycling. The two values usually belong to two teams: saying which one changes is part of the verdict.
6. DO NOT raise the memory limit. No effect on the cause, and the restart it triggers will hide the symptom until the pool fills up again. That is exactly what cost 40 minutes on INC-2024-0312.
7. Verify the fix OFF-PEAK. A verification under load proves nothing.","revision":"2025-04-02","services":"billing-api, payments-api, checkout-api","symptoms":"Intermittent 5xx errors (502/504) not correlated with traffic volume, often off-peak. Container RSS growing steadily and monotonically. No restart, no OOMKill, liveness and readiness probes green. In the application logs: 'connection reset by peer', not 'timeout'.","tags":"pool connections rds proxy dbproxy idleclienttimeout recycling db_pool_idle_timeout_seconds","title":"Connection pool exhaustion - idle timeout mismatch on the network path","verification":"db_connection_wait_seconds goes back under 50 ms and RSS stabilises. Verification is conclusive only after a low-traffic period at least twice as long as the shortest idle timeout of the path.","warning":"READ BEFORE APPLYING - Two traps, and both give the illusion of a fix. (1) THIS DEFECT IS INVISIBLE UNDER LOAD: when traffic is sustained, no connection stays idle long enough to be cut. The symptom stops by itself when traffic comes back; do not conclude it is solved. (2) ANY RESTART HIDES THE SYMPTOM: a fresh pool holds no dead connection, so errors stop at once, then come back once the pool has filled up and gone idle again. A fix that restarts the pod (raising a memory limit, for example) will therefore seem to work. Never conclude on an observation made right after a restart."}
